# Draft:A. B. Venkateswara Rao

A. B. Venkateswara Rao
A. B. Venkateswara Rao is a retired Indian Police Service (IPS) officer who served in the Andhra Pradesh Police. He is a 1989-batch officer and served as Additional Director General of Police (Intelligence) in Andhra Pradesh.
Career
A. B. Venkateswara Rao served the Andhra Pradesh Police for nearly three decades in various operational and administrative roles. He was appointed as Additional Director General of Police (Intelligence), a key position responsible for internal security and intelligence coordination in the state.
In 2019, after a change in the Andhra Pradesh government, Rao was suspended from service and faced allegations related to the procurement of surveillance equipment. The Andhra Pradesh High Court later quashed the corruption case, stating that there was no sufficient material to proceed with prosecution.
Subsequently, the Andhra Pradesh government dropped all proceedings against Rao after the High Court quashed both the FIR and charge sheet filed against him.
The developments surrounding the case and the political controversy were widely reported in national media.
Public life
After his retirement, Rao has participated in public meetings and discussions related to governance, administration, and policing. His remarks and experiences as a senior police officer have been reported by mainstream Indian media.
